fullPassage: Consistent individual differences in behavior within populations, also known as personality, are attracting the attention of many evolutionary biologists. One of the reasons why personality is interesting from an evolutionary perspective is that behaving in a consistent way across a variety of contexts or through time seems maladaptive At some point, a mismatch between an individual’s behavior and the optimal strategy for a given situation may be expected. For example an individual that is consistently uninhibited and bold will at some point incur an elevated risk of predation the optimal individual should be bold only when it makes sense to be bold, and adjust its behavior when the situation changes. However personality implies that individuals are limited in their behavioral plasticity the individuals that are, for example, particularly active in the absence of predation risk are also those that are most active in the presence of predation risk From an evolutionary perspective, personality may be harmful as optimal individuals should adapt their behavior to changing circumstances, yet the persistence of personality suggests a limit to behavioral flexibility. consistent unchanging constant maladaptive counterproductive disadvantageous optimal ideal most suitable best adjust adapt modify alter plasticity flexibility adaptability S V S V S V S V S V For example, However
